_comment: Gate 4 sizing: what real SRAM macros would actually buy. Measured by synthesising railnet_top twice against the same Liberty, changing only how inferred memories are handled. Committed because results/ and build/ are gitignored.
question: The area in gate3_evidence.json excludes memories. How much do those memories cost if they are not macros?
reading: Memories dominate the design: implemented as flip-flops they are 9.4x the entire logic area. Real SRAM macros would displace about 2.06 mm2. This is the strongest argument for closing Gate 4, and it is a cost the project's earlier area claims never accounted for.

artifacts_missing: sky130_sram_4kbyte_1rw1r_32x1024_8 - modelled by hardware/asic/sky130_sram_macros.v but absent from the sky130A PDK

fit_analysis.16b x 1024: the only clean fit - two 8x1024 macros side by side; these are also the largest arrays, so they carry most of the 2.06 mm2
fit_analysis.32b x 32: smallest macro is 32x256, an 8x waste; flip-flops are likely cheaper here
fit_analysis.27b x 128: no sensible match in the PDK

why_not_integrated_yet.also: No module instantiates any SRAM macro today; hardware/asic/sky130_sram_macros.v is a behavioural model of macros that were never wired in.

not_performed: wiring any PDK macro into the RTL
re-shaping the inferred memories to macro-friendly geometries
placement or routing with macros present
